sourceBoundary.instructionBoundary: The recordings are evidence, not requirement documents. User request and locked factory artifacts remain authoritative.
sourceBoundary.noCopyRule: Transfer abstract feedback principles only; do not copy third-party assets, names, UI expression, layouts or tuning values.

whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.referenceEvidence: Waffle-like panels, fruit/round targets, layered cake stacks, colored columns and spring-like hazards are immediately distinguishable by silhouette and material.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.oursEvidence: Default runtime mostly exposes programmatic box/cone/support geometry; foodStyle exists in data and presentation but does not yet create the same readable interaction vocabulary across the whole course.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.missingFactoryGate: Object-role visual semantic gate across early/mid/late natural samples.

whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.referenceEvidence: A successful cut visibly produces a separated piece, score increment, motion continuation and a new route state before the next target.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.oursEvidence: Default path records cuts, produces split halves, particles and a CSS feedback pop, but the chain is quieter and less materially differentiated.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.missingFactoryGate: Natural exact-object cut trace must prove anticipation → contact → separation → score → next decision.

whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.referenceEvidence: Visible knife arc/trail, impact flash/particles, object break, floating score and camera framing overlap in a short readable moment.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.oursEvidence: Main runtime has cut particles, a short impact flash and a feedback pop; the richer slash-trail/hit-stop/camera-trauma implementation exists in poc-3d.ts but is not the default game journey.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.missingFactoryGate: Runtime-product wiring gate must reject a feedback feature that only exists in a POC/compatibility path.

whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.referenceEvidence: The second recording shows an explicit CONTINUE? overlay with a clear no-thanks/yes decision after failure.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.oursEvidence: Our default terminal has replay and progression, but no equivalent recovery choice; Bonus test entry is exposed before failure and is not a player-facing recovery decision.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.missingFactoryGate: Default journey must distinguish player recovery choice from debug/test entry.

whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.referenceEvidence: The wall carries many surface labels and remains in the same frame as knife contact and impact feedback.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.oursEvidence: Current repair has opaque contiguous wall geometry and HUD labels; wall-surface labels and close camera composition remain incomplete.
whatTheyHaveThatWeDoNot.missingFactoryGate: Exact lane label + knife-wall relation + impact screenshot at desktop and 390x844.

cutFeelDecomposition.missing: The target does not consistently announce material, cut direction and consequence before contact.
No default-path hit-stop/camera-trauma proof; contact lacks a distinct weight change from ordinary motion.

referenceSignals: large, readable pieces split and travel
cutFeelDecomposition.missing: Fragment motion and silhouettes are less visually legible at the gameplay camera; style variation is not yet as immediate as the reference.
The reference makes per-cut earnings and the persistent total update simultaneously; our generic +value and score counter do not yet establish one authored currency reward beat.
No explicit recover/decline moment; debug Bonus control competes with the normal journey.

whatToAddToOurFactory: Add a realtime earnings contract: every cut and finish multiplier must emit a local delta plus persistent-total update in one natural trace; a final score assertion alone is insufficient.

Make cut-feel a runtime-wired product gate: slash trail, impact flash, bounded hit-stop, camera response, particles, fragment separation, score pop and next-target reveal must all be observed on the default path.
Require a three-object natural sample (early/mid/late) with objectId-specific evidence for anticipation, contact, separation and recovery.
Add a material/role visual contract so cuttable targets, hard surfaces and hazards are distinguishable without helper text.
Add a terminal recovery contract: replay is primary; any continue/recovery choice must be a normal player affordance, never a debug/test button.
Promote the finish-wall surface-label and camera-composition gate from retro recommendation to formal perceptual acceptance criteria.

implementationEvidenceGap.risk: A passing POC feedback trace must not be used as proof that the default game journey has the same cutting feel.
implementationEvidenceGap.requiredAction: Either wire the approved feel stack into the default runtime or label the POC explicitly as non-product evidence and keep the product gate BLOCKED.

nextRoute: formal-fixer triage for default-path cut-feel and finish-wall presentation; no code change performed in this retro.
claimBoundary: Web-lite experience/process retro only; native platform packaging and real-device behavior remain unverified.
